no_intercluster_link.rule: ONE hub, TWO independent clusters. There is NO Lake Washington ↔ Puget Sound water link in ANY phase — do not render, imply, or reserve a connector line between the clusters, and route zero geometry through the Ballard Locks or the Ship Canal.
no_intercluster_link.reason: Inventory verdict: the only water connection is the Lake Washington Ship Canal — a blanket 7-knot zone end-to-end (SMC 16.20.130) — through the Ballard Locks, which are first-come queue-based with small-lock cycles of ~10–15 min best case and documented waits of 1–4 hours on busy days, plus 4-kn approach zones. copy.hero: Two floating bridges. One lake. Zero water commute — until now. Navier is building an employer water network for Seattle: 20-seat electric hydrofoils crossing Lake Washington — Leschi to Bellevue in 12–15 minutes, Kirkland and Renton linked through Meydenbauer Bay — plus a second network on Elliott Bay connecting West Seattle, the downtown waterfront, and the Expedia campus, growing to Bainbridge Island and Des Moines.

sections.why_seattle: This region already commutes by water: Washington State Ferries' Bainbridge run is a daily 35-minute workhorse, Kitsap's fast ferries carried more than 850,000 riders in 2024, and the King County Water Taxi tops 700,000 boardings a year. Yet Lake Washington — ringed by jobs on both shores — has no scheduled water service at all. Its only crossings are two congested floating bridges, with peak SR-520 tolls of $4.90–$6.90 and a 51-minute planning time for a trip the water covers in about 15. The lake is open, legal, fast water; it just has no boats.
sections.how_it_works: Employers commit seat blocks on a corridor. When a corridor reaches 60–80 committed seats, it launches. Seats are guaranteed, quiet, working commutes on zero-emission electric hydrofoils.
sections.network_lake: Two launch lines meet at Meydenbauer Bay: the Bridge Bypass Line (Leschi ↔ Bellevue, 12–15 min indicative — the I-90/SR-520 bypass) and the Boeing Line (Kirkland ↔ Meydenbauer Bay ↔ Renton, ~25–30 min end-to-end, landing at the walk-tier waterfront doorstep of Boeing Renton and the Southport offices). Downtown Bellevue and Amazon's Bellevue towers are a 15–20 minute uphill walk or a short shuttle from the Meydenbauer dock. Phase 2 adds a Kirkland ↔ Leschi direct (15–18 min indicative) with a Carillon Point stop and a shuttle connection toward Microsoft Redmond.
sections.network_sound: On Elliott Bay, the Expedia Shuttle links West Seattle (Seacrest), the downtown waterfront at Bell Harbor Pier 66, and Elliott Bay Marina — a 10–15 minute waterfront walk from Expedia's 40-acre campus. Phase 2 adds a direct Bainbridge ↔ Elliott Bay Marina overlay with no downtown transfer, and revives the Des Moines ↔ Bell Harbor run that a 2022 passenger-ferry pilot already proved marina-to-marina. Later phases explore Kingston, Edmonds, and a Gig Harbor ↔ Tacoma shuttle. We serve landings the public ferries don't — as a complement to the region's ferry system, never a replacement.
sections.two_networks: The lake and the Sound operate as two independent networks. The only water between them runs through the Ballard Locks — a first-come lock queue, not a commuter connection — so we don't pretend there's a boat from Bellevue to Bainbridge. There isn't, and there won't be.
sections.timing: Targeting first service no earlier than end-2027. Every travel time shown is indicative until routes are finalized with harbor authorities, and lake times include the slow near-shore approach zones at each dock.
sections.loi_ask: Register interest with a non-binding letter of intent. It costs nothing and reserves nothing — it tells us which corridors to launch first.
